chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever repents one year before his death, Allah will accept his repentance.' Then he said: 'Indeed, a year is a long time.' Whoever repents one month before his death, Allah will accept his repentance.' Then he said: 'Indeed, a month is a long time.' Whoever repents one day before his death, Allah will accept his repentance.' Then he said: 'Indeed, a day is a long time.' Whoever repents before he sees (death), Allah will accept his repentance.'
ai.seo_question: How close to death can one repent and still have their repentance accepted in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi employs a rhetorical device of gradual compression—moving from a year to a single day—to illustrate the boundless nature of divine mercy, ensuring believers do not despair of Allah's forgiveness regardless of how close death approaches. In Shia scholarship, this is often linked to the concept of 'tawbah al-nas' (repentance of the general public) and serves as a spiritual encouragement to maintain hope (rajā') until the very last breath. The narration underscores that repentance is not merely a legal formality but a transformative state of being that Allah accepts even when the opportunity seems fleeting.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who repents one year before his death, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Accept his repentance’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A year is a lot. The one who repents by a month before his death, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Accept his repentance’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A month is a lot. The one who repents one Friday (week) before his death, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Accept his repentance’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A Friday (week) is a lot. The one who repents one day before his death, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Accept his repentance’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A day is a lot. The one who repents before he sees (the death), Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Accept his repentance’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from those whom he has mentioned (in his book) from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘If one repents one year before his death, Allah accepts his repentance.’ Then he said, ‘One year is a long time. Whoever repents one month before his death Allah accepts his repentance.’ Then he said, ‘One month is a long time. Whoever repents one week before his death, Allah accepts his repentance.’ Then he said, ‘One week is a long time. Whoever repents one day before his death, Allah accepts his repentance.’ Then he said, ‘One day is a long time. Whoever repents before he sees (the consequences), Allah accepts his repentance.’”
